messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: Elevated 5xx rate detected for inference endpoints in aws us-west-2 starting at 2026-03-15T02:17:56Z. Route53 healthchecks showing increased latency and intermittent SERVFAILs. Creating incident #INC-2026-0315-uw2. Paging oncall.

alice (oncall): I see it. Paging SRE now. @ben are you able to take?

ben (sre): oncall here, ack. I'm seeing ELB target health flapping and a spike in ENI attach/detach errors in us-west-2. Initial impact: ~30% of requests getting 5xx or timeouts, p95 latency jumped to ~1.2s for text-generation routes.

carla (eng-runtime): adding runtime view — KV cache miss rate for us-west-2 also up 40%. Could be partial network partition to some AZs.

ben (sre): good catch. I'm running quick triage, collecting awsb logs.

ben (sre): aws-status-bot posted: "Investigating: EC2 API errors reported in US-WEST-2 (kcu) — some customers reporting attach/detach failures"

alice (oncall): severity? Customer-facing impact for hosted API customers in us-west-2 only. Global fallback should still route to us-west-1 and us-east-1 for compatible models, but traffic shaping may not be on for all tenants. Declaring Sev2 for now.

dave (support): we have two customers reporting increased errors — ticket #SUP-4221 and #SUP-4222. Both on Dedicated in us-west-2. Flagging to enterprise CS.

carla (eng-runtime): immediate mitigation ideas: 1) disable serving in affected AZs within us-west-2 2) nudge smart-routing to avoid us-west-2 3) enable cross-region fallback for high-traffic routes.

ben (sre): working on step 1. Listing ELB targetgroups to find affected targets.\
ben (sre): Command:
```bash
aws elbv2 describe-target-health --target-group-arn arn:aws:elasticloadbalancing:us-west-2:123456:targetgroup/ri-infer-svc/abcd1234
```

ben (sre): Output shows multiple targets UNHEALTHY with reason "Target responded with an error" and several INACTIVE because of ENI problems.

carla (eng-runtime): Ben, if you remove targets in the bad AZs we should avoid routing to them, but need to ensure autoscaling doesn't immediately replace with same AZ. Consider updating AZ balance to prefer other AZs.

ben (sre): I'm editing ELB weights to 0 for the two subnets in us-west-2a/us-west-2b that show the flapping targets.

ben (sre): Command I executed:
```bash
aws elbv2 modify-target-group-attributes --target-group-arn <tg> --attributes Key=slow_start.duration_seconds,Value=0 Key=deregistration_delay.timeout_seconds,Value=30
```

alice (oncall): After you do that, update smart-routing policy in the control plane to mark us-west-2 as degraded so that new requests route away. Carla, can you push that?

carla (eng-runtime): On it. Patching routing policy via console and will confirm with API.

carla (eng-runtime): API call:
```http
POST /api/v1/routing/policies/degrade
{ "region": "us-west-2", "reason": "networking-eni-errors", "expires_in": 3600 }
```

carla (eng-runtime): response: 200 OK — global control plane will route new requests away from us-west-2. Existing connections may still see errors for a short window.

ben (sre): Observing traffic shift. 5xx rate for us-west-2 decreased from 30% to 8% over the last 3 minutes. p95 latency for global requests back down to ~400ms.

dave (support): pinging impacted enterprise customers saying: "We're aware of elevated errors in us-west-2 and have applied a regional routing fallback. We'll monitor and follow up" — customers acknowledged.

elaine (pm): Can we quantify how many customers were routed off us-west-2? Need to estimate any cost/latency regression.

carla (eng-runtime): Quick numbers: ~18% of traffic in platform was originating from us-west-2 for the affected model family. After fallback, ~15% moved to us-west-1 and ~3% to us-east-1. Average added latency for those requests ~110ms.

ben (sre): I'm still seeing residual route53 SERVFAILs for some delegated zones in us-west-2 region. Opening ticket with AWS Support — requesting escalation to networking team.

ben (sre): aws support case created: 123-uw2-network-20260315. Noted ENI API errors, ELB target flapping, Route53 healthcheck SERVFAILs. Asking for ETA.

aws-status-bot: AWS Notice (copied from status): "We're investigating elevated API error rates in US-WEST-2 related to EC2 networking provisioning. Some customers may experience transient instance attachment or ENI provisioning failures."

alice (oncall): Handoff: Ben, please continue incident lead for next 45 minutes. I'll stay nearby for exec comms. Ben, when you hand off to the normal SRE rotation, make sure to include the aws case and the exact ELB target modifications.

ben (sre): Acknowledged. I'll create a runbook note in the incident thread and tag the oncoming oncall.

ben (sre): runbook note (paste):
- initial detection: high 5xx in us-west-2
- actions taken: set ELB weights to 0 for affected subnets, modified routing policy to degrade us-west-2, created AWS support case 123-uw2-network-20260315
- current impact: degraded but routing fallback applied; error rate ~6-9% for legacy connections; new requests routed away
- next steps: monitor AWS updates, consider tenant-level emergency DB failover for Dedicated customers if errors persist

carla (eng-runtime): We should also run a controlled canary to ensure we can flip traffic back without regression once AWS resolves. I'll prepare a canary plan.

dave (support): Support update sent to impacted customers: "We have applied regional routing fallbacks. Please expect reduced errors, and we'll notify you when we fully restore us-west-2."

ben (sre): Update: AWS support responded: "Engineering investigating ENI provisioning subsystem, no ETA yet." They've asked for customer logs which we've uploaded.

alice (oncall): I'll draft a short status message for the status page and #general. Ben, tag me when you hand off.

ben (sre): Handing off active lead to @carla for routing/policy monitoring at 1772013000. I'll remain in thread for followups and to coordinate with AWS.

carla (eng-runtime): Taking lead. Monitoring metrics and routing. Will run canary once AWS indicates green.

aws-status-bot: AWS Update: "Partial mitigation observed. ENI API errors decreasing. Continue monitoring."

carla (eng-runtime): Noting metrics: 5xx now ~3-5% in us-west-2, global p95 ~350ms. Preparing canary to gradually re-enable US-WEST-2 in 10 minutes.

carla (eng-runtime): Canary plan snippet:
```bash
# step 1: enable 5% of traffic to us-west-2 via routing override
# step 2: monitor 1m p50/p95 and 5xx
# step 3: if stable, increase 25% each 2 minutes
```

ben (sre): AWS support updated case: "Tracking resolution, may take up to 2 hours to fully clear for some customers."

alice (oncall): Thanks team. I'll send post-incident comms template after we close. Keeping incident open until us-west-2 fully healthy and ELB targetgroups stable.

carla (eng-runtime): Canary started at 1772013200 — currently 5% traffic. No uptick in errors after 4 minutes. Increasing to 30%.

carla (eng-runtime): Traffic increase looks OK. AWS reporting continued improvement.

ben (sre): I'll leave monitoring alerts at lower thresholds for another hour.

dave (support): I'll follow up with affected Enterprise customers and share the AWS case link for transparency.

alice (oncall): Closing notes: root cause suspected EC2 networking provision/ENI subsystem in us-west-2. Mitigation: regional routing fallback, ELB target weight adjustments, AWS escalation. Postmortem to include timeline and a proposal to auto-degrade region when Route53 healthchecks cross threshold.

carla (eng-runtime): I'll kick off the postmortem doc and link the runbook changes.

ben (sre): Logging incident close when AWS confirms full recovery. For now, incident status: mitigated.

aws-status-bot: AWS Final Update: "Issue resolved for most customers in US-WEST-2. Some residual propagation for health checks may continue."

carla (eng-runtime): us-west-2 targetgroups healthy now. I reconciled ELB weights back to normal.

alice (oncall): All right — marking last_message_ts = 1772013450. Great work everyone.
